In LINE, after simplifying the second-order proximity objective, the authors use the squared Euclidean distance between the context embedding of a vertex and the embedding of its observed context vertex, i.e. \(d(\mathbf{u}_i, \mathbf{u}'_j)=\|\mathbf{u}'_j-\mathbf{u}_i\|_2^2\). The resulting objective is
\[
O_2 = -\sum_{(i,j)\in E} w_{ij}\,\log p_2(v_j\mid v_i),
\]
with
\[
p_2(v_j\mid v_i)=\frac{\exp(\mathbf{u}'_j\cdot \mathbf{u}_i)}{\sum_{k=1}^{|V|}\exp(\mathbf{u}'_k\cdot \mathbf{u}_i)}.
\]
Equivalently, using the negative-sampling approximation, it is optimized via the logistic loss on the dot product between \(\mathbf{u}_i\) and \(\mathbf{u}'_j\).
confidence_reasoning: This matches the LINE paper’s simplified second-order proximity formulation and the standard softmax objective, though exact notation can vary slightly across presentations.
